deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Gauss studies a function φ given by power series. He sums two series at the argument 10. The first is 1 + 8.3333333 + 3.4722222 + 0.2755732 + 0.0068347 + … = 13.0880328, with successive term ratios 10²/12, 10²/240, 10²/1260, 10²/4032, i.e. 10²/((2k)²((2k)²−1)). The second sums to 13.1518250. Their difference, 0.0637922, is φ'(10). He then writes the local expansion φ(10+x) = 0.2288438 + 0.0637922x − 0.0146318x² − 0.0000878x³ + 0.0001327x⁴. In it, φ''(10) = −0.0292636, which corrects the cancelled '−0.0029263'. On this page he moves to the argument 7.5, where φ changes sign. The aim is to locate the zero of φ.

(1) Local cubic model. He sets
φ(7.5+x) = a + b·x + α·x² + β·x³,
with a = φ(7.5) = −0.0146336 and b = φ'(7.5) = 0.1278546. These were evidently computed elsewhere. b = 0.1278546 also appears on the next page under 'φ''.

(2) Attempt to fix α and β by collocation (left unfinished). A first condition 'α + β = −0.0115659' is written and then struck through. α + β is what one gets by matching at x = 1, i.e. φ(8.5) − a − b; the previous page contains 0.1132210 = b + a. It is replaced by two templates whose right-hand sides are left blank:
- α + (3/4)β = … This is (φ'(7.5+½) − b)/1, the derivative condition at x = ½: b + 2α(½) + 3β(¼) = φ'(8).
- (1/4)α + (1/8)β = … This is the value condition at x = ½: a + b/2 + α/4 + β/8 = φ(8).
My reading is that he intended to fit α and β to φ(8) and φ'(8). The page does not complete this.

(3) Working quadratic. He settles on a quadratic model:
φ(7.5+x) ≈ −0.0146336 + 0.1278546x − 0.0150961x².
Here α = −0.0150961 is plausibly φ''(7.5)/2, by analogy with −0.0146318 = φ''(10)/2 on the previous page. The page does not show how this value was obtained.

(4) Root by fixed-point iteration. Setting the quadratic to zero gives
x = 0.0146336 / (0.1278546 − 0.0150961x).
Iterating:
- x₀ = 0.0146336/0.1278546 ≈ 0.11446 (my reconstruction, not written).
- The denominator becomes 0.1278546 − 0.0150961·0.11446 ≈ 0.1261268. The scratch figure '12612' is this value.
- The long division 14.6336 ÷ 12612 (remainders 2021…, 76…) gives x₁ ≈ 0.1160.
The zero of φ is therefore at about 7.5 + 0.1160 = 7.616. The next page indeed works with 7.62.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. The denominator 0.1278546 − 0.0150961·0.11446 = 0.126127 ('12612') and the quotient 0.0146336/0.126127 = 0.11602 ('1160') are both correct.
The quotient 0.1160 agrees with the exact smaller root of the quadratic, 0.11604.
The struck-out condition α+β = −0.0115659 and the two collocation equations are left without right-hand sides. The cubic coefficient β is never determined.

The origin of α = −0.0150961 is not shown on the page. It is not equal to the values a quadratic fitted to φ(10) or φ'(10) would give (−0.01219 and −0.01281 respectively), so it presumably comes from a separately computed φ''(7.5).
